αἴης: αἶα — land, earth; gen. sg., epic by-form of γαῖα

αὖ: αὖ — again, in turn, back; adv., shorter form of αὖτε
αὖτ: αὖτε (elided αὖτ’) — again, in turn, moreover; epic adv./conj.
αὖτε: αὖτε — again, in turn, on the other hand; adv.
αὖτις: αὖτις — back, again, once more; adv. (= αὖθις)
βάλλετο: βάλλω — throw, cast; mid. throw on oneself, sling; impf. 3 sg. mid., unaugmented (= ἐβάλλετο): ’he slung on’

βασιλῆα: βασιλεύς — king; acc. sg., epic βασιλῆα (= Attic βασιλέα)

βῆ: βαίνω — go, walk, step; aor. 3 sg., root aorist, unaugmented (= ἔβη): ’went, strode’

γαστέρα: γαστήρ — belly, stomach; fem. acc. sg.
γαῖα: γαῖα — earth, land; fem. nom. sg. (epic = Attic γῆ)
γε: γε — at least, in fact, indeed; limiting/emphatic particle
γενέσθαι: γίγνομαι — become, be born; aor. inf.: ’to have been born’ · also of time, ’come, arrive, come to pass’ (πρὶν δωδεκάτην γε γενέσθαι ’before the twelfth day should come’) · also with a dat., ’befall, come upon’ (πῆμα γενέσθαι ’woe to come upon us’)
γλαυκῶπις: γλαυκῶπις — epithet of Athena: ’gleaming-eyed’ (or ’owl-eyed’; sense uncertain); fem. nom. sg.
γλυκὺς: γλυκύς — sweet; masc. nom. sg. (γλυκὺς αἰών ’sweet life’)
γούνατ: γόνυ (pl. γούνατα) — knee; neut. acc. pl., elided (γούνατ’ = γούνατα)
γυναικῶν: γυνή — woman; fem. gen. pl., partitive with δῖα: ’heavenly-one of women’ · also partitive with ἀρίστη: ’best of women’ · also possessive gen. with a noun: ἔργα γυναικῶν ’the works of women’
δέπας: δέπας — cup, drinking-cup; neut. nom./acc. sg.
δέπαϊ: δέπας — cup; neut. dat. sg., epic uncontracted δέπαϊ, its ending sounded as a separate syllable (= Attic δέπᾳ)
δήμῳ: δῆμος — district, land, people; dat. sg.
δίδου: δίδωμι — give; pres. imper. 2 sg.: ’give!’ · also impf. 3 sg., epic (= ἐδίδου): ’she gave’ (of the Muse)
δαίμων: δαίμων — a god, some divine power (vague, unspecified); masc. nom. sg.

δηλήμονα: δηλήμων — destroyer, harmer; masc. acc. sg., in apposition
δηρὸν: δηρόν — for a long time, long; neut. acc. sg. used as adv. (accusative of duration)

δοκέεις: δοκέω — seem, think; pres. 2 sg., uncontracted (= Attic δοκεῖς)
δύω: δύο — two; numeral, epic by-form δύω, indeclinable

δῖα: δῖος — heavenly, divine, illustrious; fem. nom. sg., epithet of goddesses and heroes
δῖος: δῖος — heavenly, divine, illustrious; masc. nom. sg., epithet of heroes (= fem. δῖα)
δῶμα: δῶμα — house, hall, dwelling; acc. sg. · also nom. sg. (identical neut. form), subject of a verb: ’the house’

εἴκων: εἴκω — yield, give way (+ dat.); pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’yielding’
εἴποιμι: εἶπον (aor. of λέγω/φημί) — say, tell; aor. opt. 1 sg., potential with ἄν: ’I would say’
εὐρυνόμη: Εὐρυνόμη — Eurynome, the housekeeper of Odysseus’s house; fem. nom. sg.
εὖτ: εὖτε (elided εὖτ’) — when, whenever; temporal conj.
εὗδε: εὕδω — sleep; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented: ’was sleeping, slept’
ζεύς: Ζεύς — Zeus, king of the gods; nom. sg.
θεάων: θεά — goddess; gen. pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic θεῶν)
θεοί: θεός — god; nom. pl. · also voc. pl. (same form): ’you gods!’
θεοὶ: θεός — god; nom. pl. · also voc. pl. (same form): ’you gods!’
θρόνου: θρόνος — chair, seat; masc. gen. sg.
θυμός: θυμός — heart, spirit; masc. nom. sg. · also life, the breath of life
θυμὸν: θυμός — heart, spirit, soul; acc. sg. · also the life that leaves the body: ’life’ (μελιηδέα θυμὸν ἀπηύρα ’took away (my) honey-sweet life’)
θυμῷ: θυμός — heart, spirit, soul; dat. sg.
θῆκε: τίθημι — put, place, make; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔθηκε)
θῆκεν: τίθημι — put, place; aor. 3 sg. · also ’make (someone a certain way)’, with double acc.: ’made him (taller)’
κάλλεϊ: κάλλος — beauty; neut. dat. sg., epic κάλλεϊ (= Attic κάλλει)
κάρτεϊ: κάρτος — strength, might (= Attic κράτος); neut. dat. sg., epic, with εἴκων: ’(yielding) to might’

κέρδιον: κερδίων — more profitable, better; neut. nom. sg., comparative of κέρδος
κακὸν: κακός — bad, evil; masc./neut. acc. sg.: ’by an evil (fate)’, inner acc. with μόρον · also neut. nom. sg., subject of an impersonal verb (τι … κακὸν … μελέτω ’let no evil thing be a care’) · also neut. acc. sg. as a plain substantive, direct object: ’harm, evil’ (κακὸν ἀλλοδαποῖσι φέροντες ’bringing harm to men of other lands’) · also neut. acc. sg., attributive with ἦμαρ: ’evil’ (κακὸν ἦμαρ ’the evil day’) · also masc. acc. sg., predicative: ’base, cowardly’ (κακὸν καὶ ἀνήνορα ’base and unmanned’) · also neut. acc. sg. attributive with πῆμα: ’evil’ (πῆμα κακὸν ’evil harm’) · also neut. nom. sg., predicate with an infinitive as subject: κακὸν … βάζειν ’(it is) bad to speak’ · also neut. acc. sg. governed by ἐς: ’into evil’ (ἐς κακὸν … βάλῃσθα) · also neut. acc. sg. subject of an infinitive: ’an evil’ (κακὸν ἔμμεναι ’that an evil is’) · also neut. nom. sg., subject of εἴη: ’evil’ (μή τι κακὸν … εἴη ’and may no evil be’) · also neut. acc. sg., attributive with ῥάκος: ’vile’ (ῥάκος ἄλλο κακὸν ’another, a vile rag’) · also neut. nom. sg., subject of a finite verb: ’an evil’ (ἐπεὶ κακὸν ἔμπεσεν οἴκῳ ’since an evil fell upon the house’) · also neut. nom. sg., predicate with γενοίμην: ’a bane, an evil (to them)’ · also masc. acc. sg. as a plain substantive, direct object: ’a base man’ (κακὸς κακὸν ἡγηλάζει)
κακῶς: κακός — bad, evil; adv.: ’wickedly, shamefully’ · also ’miserably, in misery’ (ὀψὲ κακῶς ἔλθοι ’may he come late, in misery’)
καλὰ: καλός — beautiful, fair, fine; neut. acc. pl. · also neut. acc. pl. used adverbially: ’handsomely, finely’ (καλά … κήδεαι ’you care so finely’) · also adverbial neut. acc. pl.: ’well, finely’ (οὐκέτι καλὰ … ἀναχωρήσειν ’no longer well’)
κανέοιο: κάνεον — basket; neut. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic κανοῦ)
κατ: κατά (elided κατ’) — down from, throughout; + gen./acc. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (κατ’ … ἕζετο = κατέζετο ’sat down’)

κε: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν) · also + subj. after εἰς ὅ, ’until’ (εἰς ὅ κε … ἐποτρύνῃ ’until … urges on’) · also + subj. in a general relative: ’whoever’ (ὅς κε πίῃ) · also + subj. in a temporal clause: ’whenever, as soon as’ (ὅτε … κε θάνῃσιν; ἐπεί κε … λίπῃ) · also + subj. in a purpose clause after ὄφρα: ’so that’ (ὄφρα κε … ἀκούσῃς) · also + subj. in the protasis after εἰ: ’if ever’ (εἰ δέ κε λίσσηαι ’but if you beg’) · also + aor. indic., unreal past: ’would have’ (καὶ νύ κε … βάλεν ’and she would have hurled’) · also + subj. in a disjunctive statement of what may happen: ’may’ (ἤ κε θάνωμεν ’either we may die’) · also + opt., potential: ’would’ (καί κε … μαχοίμην ’I would fight’) · also + subj. in a relative clause of purpose: ’who are to’ (οἵ κε … ἀγγείλωσι ’who are to announce’) · also + fut. indic. κεδνὴ: κεδνός — careful, trusty; fem. nom. sg.
κεν: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν) · also + secondary indic. κεφαλῇ: κεφαλή — head; fem. dat. sg. · also periphrasis for the person: ’Achilles himself’ (Ἀχιλλῆος κεφαλῇ, dative of the person grieved for)
κεῖνον: κεῖνος — that, that one; demonstrative pron., epic (= Attic ἐκεῖνος); masc. acc. sg.
κεῖνος: κεῖνος — that, that one; demonstrative pron., epic (= Attic ἐκεῖνος); masc. nom. sg.
κλέος: κλέος — fame, renown, report; neut. nom. sg. · also neut. acc. sg. (same form), direct object: μέγα κλέος ἤρατο ’won great fame’; κλέος φέρειν ’bring report’
κλιθῆναι: κλίνω — lie down, recline; aor. pass. inf.: ’to lie down’
κνίσης: κνῖσα (epic κνίση) — savour of burning fat; fem. gen. sg., Ionic η (= Attic κνίσης): ’of the fat’
κούρῃ: κούρη — girl, maiden, daughter (Attic κόρη); dat. sg.
κτήματα: κτῆμα — possession, property; neut. nom./acc. pl.
κῆρα: κήρ — doom, fate of death; fem. acc. sg.
λαῶν: λαός — people, host; masc. gen. pl., governed by ἄνασσε ’was lord over’ · also gen. with a noun: ’of the people’ (ποιμένα λαῶν ’shepherd of the people’) · also governed by ἐκ: ἔκ ... λαῶν ’from the people’ · also partitive gen. after a relative: οἵ ... λαῶν ἡμετέρων ’those of our people who’ · also partitive gen. after an adjective of rank: πάντων ἀριδείκετε λαῶν ’most distinguished of all the people’ · also gen. governed by πρόσθεν: ’before (the city and) the people’
λευκώλενοι: λευκώλενος — white-armed; fem. voc. pl. (of the maids)
λεχέεσσι: λέχος — bed, couch; neut. dat. pl., epic -έεσσι
λιπαρὰ: λιπαρός — glistening, shining; neut. acc. pl.
λυγρὰ: λυγρός — grievous, baneful, miserable; neut. acc. pl. (grave, mid-clause form): ’grievous things’
λύθεν: λύω — loosen, release, undo; aor. pass. 3 pl., epic unaugmented (= Attic ἐλύθησαν)
λύτο: λύω — loose, undo; aor. pass. 3 sg., unaugmented root-aorist form (= ἐλύθη): ’was loosed, gave way’
μάκαρες: μάκαρ — blessed, happy (esp. of the gods); masc. nom. pl. · also voc. pl. in address: μάκαρες θεοί ’blessed gods!’
μάλ: μάλα (elided μάλ’) — very, very much, exceedingly; adv.
μάλα: μάλα — very, very much, exceedingly; adv.
μάλιστ: μάλα — very, much; superl. adv. μάλιστα, elided (μάλιστ’ = μάλιστα): ’most of all, especially’
μάλιστα: μάλα — very, much; superl. adv. μάλιστα: ’most of all, especially’ · also ’for the most part, mostly’ (μάλιστα ἦμαρ ’the greater part of the day’)
μέν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ (the acute μέν is kept before a following enclitic; elsewhere μὲν) · also asseverative, = μήν ’truly, indeed’ (οὐ μέν ’not indeed’) · also μένω — stay, wait; pres. imper. 2 sg., elided (μέν’ = μένε): ’stay’

μεγάλην: μέγας — great, mighty; fem. acc. sg.
μεγάροιο: μέγαρον — hall; gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
μεγάροισιν: μέγαρον — hall, great room, house; neut. dat. pl., epic -οισι(ν), plural for a single house
μελιηδέα: μελιηδής — honey-sweet; fem. acc. sg., uncontracted (adj. of two endings) · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with a masc. noun (μελιηδέα καρπόν ’honey-sweet fruit’)
μετ: μετά (elided μετ’) — among, after, in quest of; prep. + acc. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (μετ’ … βαῖνε = μετέβαινε ’followed’) · also + dat., ’among, between’ (μετ’ ἀμφοτέροισιν ’between the two of them’) · also + gen., ’among, in company with’ (μετ’ ἄλλων … ἑταίρων ’among your other companions’)

μηδ: μηδέ — and not, nor; neg. conj., elided (μηδ’ = μηδέ)
μηκέτ: μηκέτι — no longer, no more; adv., elided (μηκέτ’ = μηκέτι)
μιν: μιν — him, her, it; epic encl. acc. pron. (= Attic αὐτόν/αὐτήν/αὐτό)
μνηστήρεσσι: μνηστήρ — suitor; masc. dat. pl., epic -εσσι
μοι: ἐγώ — I; encl. dat. sg.: ’to me, for me’ · also dat. of the person affected, ’from my …’ (μοι βλεφάρων ἐξέσσυτο ὕπνος ’sleep rushed out from my eyelids’) · also dat. of possession with εἰμί: ’who are mine’ (οἵ μοι ἔασιν ’who are mine’)
μοῖραν: μοῖρα — due share, what is fitting, portion, fate; fem. acc. sg. (κατὰ μοῖραν ’according to what is fitting’)
μὲν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ · also asseverative, = μήν ’truly, indeed’: οὐ μὲν δή ’surely not’
μὴ: μή — not; negative particle in wishes, prohibitions, and purpose/fear clauses · also negating a conditional clause after εἰ: εἰ μὴ ’if not, unless’ · also negating a generic relative clause with the opt.: ὃς μὴ … ἐλάσειε ’whoever did not drive off’ · also ’lest’ in a warning, + 2 sg. fut./subj.: μὴ … ἀποτίσεαι ’lest you pay for it’
μᾶλλον: μάλα — very, much; comparative adv. μᾶλλον: ’more, rather, the more’
μῦθον: μῦθος — word, speech, thing said; acc. sg. · also a plan, scheme agreed on (τοῖον...τελέωμεν μῦθον ’let us carry out this plan’)
νέεσθαι: νέομαι — go, return home; pres. inf., epic uncontracted (= Attic νεῖσθαι)
νευστάζων: νευστάζω — nod repeatedly, make signs; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’nodding’
νηυσίν: ναῦς — ship; dat. pl., epic νηυσί(ν) (= Attic ναυσί)
νοστήσειε: νοστέω — return home; aor. opt. 3 sg., optative of hope/expectation: ’should he return’
ξεῖνε: ξεῖνος — stranger, guest-friend (epic = Attic ξένος); voc. sg.
οἱ: οἱ — encl. dat. sg. pron. ’to/for him’ (very common) · also ὁ, ἡ, τό ’he, she, it’, masc. nom. pl. ’they’ (e.g. οἱ μὲν … οἱ δέ ’some … others’) · also encl. dat. sg. fem. ’to/for her’ (ἥ οἱ ὁμηλικίη ’who was of an age with her’) · also article-like with a numeral and noun, masc. nom. pl.: ’the’ (οἱ δὲ δύω σκόπελοι ’the two crags’) · also encl. dat. sg. of a thing, ’to/for it’ (δύω δέ τέ οἱ θύραι ’and it has two doors’) · also article-like with a noun, masc. nom. pl.: ’those, the’ (οἱ πέπλοι ’the robes’) · also dat. sg. of the giver with δέχομαι: ’from him’ (οἱ ἐδέξατο ’took from him’)
οἴη: οἶος — alone, only; fem. nom. sg.
οἴκαδ: οἴκαδε (elided οἴκαδ’) — homeward, to home; adv., -δε suffix of direction
οἵ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., masc. nom. pl. · also encl. dat. sg. pron. ’to/for him’ (= οἱ, accented οἵ in this position) · also ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; masc. nom. pl. ’they’, demonstrative: οἵ γ’ ὑβρισταί ’are they violent?’
οἵῳ: οἷος — of what sort, such as; masc. dat. sg., relative (= ὁποίῳ), agreeing with an understood δίσκῳ: ’of the kind that’
οἷ: οἷος — of what kind, such as; relative/exclamatory adj., neut. nom./acc. pl. οἷα, elided (οἷ’) · also orthotone dat. sg. of the 3rd-person pronoun (= οἱ): ’to him, to her’
οἷον: οἷος — such as, of what sort; neut. as exclamatory adv.: ’how!, what a thing!’ (rough breathing; distinct from οἶος ’alone’) · also causal conj. after a verb of emotion, ’in that, that’ · also correlative ’such as, as’ (οἷον ὅτε πρώτιστον ’such as when first’) · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with τὸν Τηλεφίδην: ’what a man, such a one as’ (ἀλλ’ οἷον … κατενήρατο ’but what a man he slew’)
οὐδ: οὐδέ (elided οὐδ’) — and not, nor, not even
οὐδὲν: οὐδείς, οὐδεμία, οὐδέν — no one, nothing; neut. acc./nom. sg. used adverbially: ’not at all’ · also neut. nom. sg. as subject: ’nothing’ (οὐδὲν γλύκιον … γίγνεται ’nothing is sweeter’)
οὐκ: οὐ — not; neg. adv., form before a vowel with smooth breathing (οὐχ before a rough breathing)
οὐκέτι: οὐκέτι — no longer, not any more; adv.
οὔ: οὐ — not; neg. adv., in a question expecting the answer ’yes’ · also the plain negative adverb in a declarative statement, with no question implied: ’not’
οὕτω: οὕτω(ς) — thus, so, in this way; adv.
οὗ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., masc. gen. sg.: ’whose’ (= Attic οὗ) · also neut. gen. sg. in ἐξ οὗ ’since, from the time when’ · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own; masc. gen. sg. agreeing with a noun (οὗ πατρὸς ’her own father’s’)
πάντα: πᾶς — all, every; neut. nom./acc. pl. · also masc. acc. sg.: ’all’ (πάντα δῆμον ’all the people’) · also neut. acc. pl. adverbial: ’altogether, in every respect’ (οὐκ ἄρα πάντα νοήμονες ’not altogether sensible’)
πάντες: πᾶς — all, every; masc. nom. pl.
πάρος: πάρος — before, formerly; adv., with inf. like Attic πρίν · also a plain temporal adverb with a finite verb, not paired with an infinitive: ’formerly, in the past’ (αἳ πάρος ἦσαν ’who formerly were’) · also ’before (that)’ with a finite verb, in the past: πάρος δ’ εἰς Ἴλιον ᾤχετο ’before that he went to Ilios’
πάσσονα: παχύς — thick, stout; epic comparative πάσσων (= Attic παχύτερος), masc. acc. sg.: ’stouter’
πέδησε: πεδάω — bind, fetter; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented, tmesis with κατά (= κατέπεδησε): ’bound fast’
πήρην: πήρη — wallet, beggar’s bag; fem. acc. sg.
παιδὶ: παῖς — child, son; masc. dat. sg.
παντοίην: παντοῖος — of every kind, all sorts of; fem. acc. sg.
παρέθηκεν: παρατίθημι — set beside, serve; aor. 3 sg. (ν-movable)
παρέστη: παρίστημι — stand beside, take one’s stand by; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented
παραύδα: παραυδάω — speak soothingly, try to talk round or console; pres. imper. 2 sg.
παραὶ: παρά (epic παραί) — beside, along; prep. + dat.
παρειάων: παρειή — cheek; fem. gen. pl., epic -άων (= Attic -ῶν)
παρὰ: παρά — beside, along, from; prep. + dat./acc./gen. · also used as an adverb with no case expressed: ’beside, alongside’ (παρὰ … ἐτάνυσσε τράπεζαν ’drew a table up beside (them)’) · also + acc., ’beside, contrary to’ (παρὰ μοῖραν ’beside what is fitting’)
πατρίδα: πατρίς — native land, fatherland; fem. acc. sg. (φίλην ... πατρίδα γαῖαν ’his dear fatherland’)
πατρίδος: πατρίς — fatherland, native land; gen. sg.
παῖς: παῖς — child, son, daughter; nom. sg.
πείσεσθαι: πείθω — persuade; mid./pass. fut. inf. πείσεσθαι: ’to be persuaded, to be won over’ (οὐ πείσεσθαι ἔμελλεν ’he was not to win her over’)
πεπνυμένος: πέπνυμαι — have one’s wits about one, be prudent; perf. part. masc. nom. sg. (trad. linked to πνέω ’breathe’, though uncertain), stock epithet: ’prudent’
περ: περ — even, though; concessive particle, esp. with a participle (= Attic καίπερ) · also used to intensify an adverb or pronoun rather than concede a point: ἔνθα περ ’in the very place where, just where’ · also after εἰ, ’if indeed, even if’: εἴ περ γάρ κεν ’if indeed ever’
περίφρονι: περίφρων — circumspect, thoughtful; adj. (2-term.), fem. dat. sg., agreeing with Πηνελοπείῃ
περίφρων: περίφρων — circumspect, of sound understanding; fem. nom. sg., stock epithet of Penelope · also epithet of Arete: fem. nom. sg., ’the circumspect queen’
περὶ: περί — around, about; prep. + gen.: ’superior to, beyond’; also as adv.: ’exceedingly, surpassingly’ · also prep. + gen. in its plain sense ’about, concerning’ (περὶ πατρός ’about his father’) · also preverb in tmesis · + dat. · also + acc., of place, ’around, about’ (περὶ ἄστυ ’around the city’) · also + gen., of place, physically ’around, encircling’ (περὶ σπείους γλαφυροῖο ’around the hollow cave’), distinct from the comparative ’beyond’ sense above · also + dat. in the fixed idiom περὶ κῆρι ’exceedingly, at heart’ (περὶ κῆρι τιμήσουσιν ’will honor him at heart’) · also + dat., of place, ’around, about’ (περὶ χροῒ ’about the skin’) · also adverb of place, no case: ’round about’ (περὶ δ’ ἕρκος ἐλήλαται ’and round it a fence is driven’) · also + dat., of the thing fought over: ’over, for’ (περὶ κτεάτεσσι μαχειόμενος ’fighting over possessions’)
πεφυρμένη: φύρω — mix, mingle, soil; perf. pass. part. fem. nom. sg., + dat.: ’mingled, drenched (with tears)’
πηνελοπείῃ: Πηνελόπεια — Penelope; dat. sg., dat. of comparison · also dat. sg., indirect object: ’to Penelope’ (ἐρέοντα περίφρονι Πηνελοπείῃ ’to tell prudent Penelope’)
πηνελόπεια: Πηνελόπεια — Penelope, wife of Odysseus; nom. sg.
ποιητοῖο: ποιητός — made, built; masc. gen. sg., epic -οῖο (= Attic -οῦ): ’well-built’
πολλὰ: πολύς — much, many; neut. acc. pl.: ’many things, greatly’ · also neut. nom. pl., plain attributive adj. agreeing with a neut. pl. noun (πολλὰ ... δάκρυα ’many tears’) · also neut. acc. pl., plain attributive adj. (κτήματα πολλὰ ’many possessions’) · also neut. acc. pl. used adverbially: ’again and again’ (πολλὰ περιτροπέοντες) · also neut. nom. pl. as substantive, subject: οἷά τε πολλὰ γίγνεται ’as many things happen’
πολύμητις: πολύμητις — of many wiles, epithet of Odysseus (built on μῆτις ’cunning intelligence’); masc. nom. sg.
ποτ: ποτέ — once, at some time, ever; enclitic adv., elided (ποτ’ = ποτέ)
ποτέ: ποτέ — once, at some time, ever; encl. adv.
ποτε: ποτέ — once, at some time, formerly; enclitic adv.
προσέειπε: προσεῖπον — speak to, address; aor. 3 sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic προσεῖπε)
προσέφη: πρόσφημι — speak to, address; aor. 3 sg.
προσεφώνεεν: προσφωνέω — speak to, address; impf. 3 sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic προσεφώνει)
πρόσωπα: πρόσωπον — face; neut. acc. pl. (plural for one face)
πρὸς: πρός — towards, against, to; prep. + acc. · also a plain adverb, no case governed: ’besides, in addition’ · also + dat.: πρὸς ἀλλήλῃσιν ἔχονται ’cling close to one another’ · also + gen., ’from, under the protection of’ (πρὸς Διός εἰσιν ’are from Zeus’) · also + dat., ’against’ (ῥαίοιτο πρὸς οὔδεϊ ’be dashed against the floor’) · also + dat., ’in addition to’ (πρὸς τοῖσί τε ὕπνος ’and sleep in addition to these’) · also + gen., of direction: ’toward, on the side of’ (πρὸς Βορέαο ’toward the North Wind’) · also + gen., in an appeal: ’by (your father)’ (πρὸς πατρὸς γουνάζομαι) · also as preverb in tmesis: με πρὸς μῦθον ἔειπε = με προσέειπε μῦθον ’spoke a word to me’
πρῶτα: πρῶτος — first; neut. acc. pl. used adverbially: ’first’
πυκνὰ: πυκνός — thick, dense; neut. acc. pl. · also neut. acc. pl. used adverbially: ’thickly, closely’ (πυκνὰ ῥωγαλέην ’thickly ragged’)
πόροι: πόρον (πορεῖν) — give, furnish; aor. opt. 3 sg. (a defective aorist with no present in this sense)
πόσιος: πόσις — drinking; gen. sg. (abstract noun, distinct from πόσις ’husband’) · also πόσις — husband; masc. gen. sg. (εὐνὴν … πόσιος ’her husband’s bed’)
πύκα: πύκα — closely, snugly, firmly; adv. (πύκα ποιητοῖο ’closely built’)
σ: σύ — you (sg.); encl. acc. sg., elided (σ’ = σε): ’you’ · also σός — your, yours; neut. nom./acc. pl., elided (σ’ = σά): τὰ σ’ αὐτοῦ κήδε’ ’your own troubles’
σιγαλόεντα: σιγαλόεις — glossy, gleaming (sense uncertain); neut. nom./acc. pl. · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with χιτῶνα: ’gleaming’
σιγῇ: σιγή — silence; fem. dat. sg. used adverbially: ’in silence’
σπείσας: σπένδω — pour a libation; aor. part. act., masc. nom. sg.
σταθμὸν: σταθμός — door-post; masc. acc. sg. · also σταθμός — steading, farmstead; masc. acc. sg., object: ’the steading’ (σταθμὸν ῥύατ’ ’guarded the steading’)
στρόφος: στρόφος — twisted cord, rope; masc. nom. sg.
στῆ: ἵστημι — set, stand; aor. 3 sg., root aorist, unaugmented (= ἔστη): ’stood’
σχεδόν: σχεδόν — near, close at hand; adv.
σχομένη: ἔχω — have, hold; aor. mid. part. fem. nom. sg., here ’holding (before)’ · also ἔχομαι + dat., ’held fast by, seized with’ (ἄχεϊ σχομένη)
σύνθεο: συντίθημι — put together; mid. take to heart, mark; aor. imper. mid. 2 sg., unaugmented, epic (= Attic σύνθου)
σὺ: σύ — you (sg.); nom. sg. (grave, mid-clause form)
σῷ: σός — your, yours; masc./neut. dat. sg.
τ: τε (elided τ’) — and; ’epic τε’ also marks a standing fact · after οὔ νυ perhaps τοι ’to you’ · also in a question, an expressive epic τε with no connective force, giving a note of doubt or wonder (πῶς τε ...; ’how, pray...?’) · also in ἦ τ’ (= ἦ τε), a strengthened affirmation: ’truly, surely’ (ἦ τ’ ἂν πολὺ κέρδιον ἦεν ’it would surely have been far better’) · also after a relative of size or amount, with no connective force: ὅσην τ’ ὄρεος κορυφήν ’as large as a mountain’s peak’ · also after ἤ ’than’, with no connective force: ἤ τ’ οἰωνοί ’than birds’
τέγεος: τέγος — roof (standing for the hall); neut. gen. sg.
τέκος: τέκος — child, offspring; neut. voc. sg. (φίλον τέκος ’dear child’)
τέως: τέως — meanwhile, for a while; adv., often with μέν
τίς: τίς, τί — who? what?; interrog. pron., masc. nom. sg. · also the enclitic indefinite τις accented before a following enclitic, not interrogative: ’someone, anyone’ (ἤν τίς τοι εἴπῃσι ’if someone tells you’)
ταμίη: ταμίη — housekeeper, stewardess, woman with charge of the stores (Attic ταμία, Ionic η for α); nom. sg.
ταῦτά: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this; neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’, accented before an enclitic
ταῦτα: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this; neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’
τε: τε — and, both...and; enclitic connective; also ’epic τε’ marking a standing general truth in relative clauses
τετιημένος: τετίημαι — be grieved, be downcast (defective, perf. with pres. force); perf. part. masc. nom. sg.
τετληότι: τλάω — endure, have the heart to bear; perf. part. (τετληώς) masc./neut. dat. sg.: ’enduring’
τηλέμαχον: Τηλέμαχος — Telemachus, son of Odysseus; masc. acc. sg.
τηλίκος: τηλίκος — of such an age, so old; masc. nom. sg.
τηλεμάχου: Τηλέμαχος — Telemachus, son of Odysseus; masc. gen. sg.
τι: τις, τι — someone, something; neut. acc. sg., used adverbially with negatives ’at all’ · also adjectival indefinite: ’some, any’ (τι δήμιον ἄλλο ’some other public matter’) · also adverbial without a negative: ’in some way, in some measure’ (τι κατὰ πρῆξιν ’on some business’) · also as a substantive object, in a question: ’anything, something’ (ἦ ῥά τι ἴδμεν ’do we know anything’) · also the neut. of τις forming, with a preceding ὅ, the indefinite relative ὅ τι ’whatever, that which’ (αὔδα ὅ τι φρονέεις ’say whatever you have in mind’) · also ὅ τι as an adverbial acc. in an indirect question: ’why’ · also as a substantive object in a statement: ’something’ (καί τι ἴσασι ’they know something’)
τοίου: τοῖος — such, of such a kind; demonstrative/correlative adj., masc. gen. sg.
τοι: σύ — you (sg.); encl. dat. sg.: ’to/for you’ · also τοι, the affirming particle: ’you know, indeed’ (esp. in ἦ τοι, οὔ τοι); the two are not always easy to keep apart
τοὶ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. nom. pl.: ’they’; also relative: ’who’ · also τοι, the affirming particle (ἀλλ’ ἦ τοι ’but truly’), as the grave-accented form τοὶ
τοῖος: τοῖος — such, of such a kind; masc. nom. sg. (τοῖος ... οἷον ’such as’)
τοῦ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. gen. sg. ’of him, that one’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whose, of whom; masc. gen. sg. (τοῦ νῶι θεοῦ ὣς τερπόμεθ’ αὐδῇ ’whose voice we delight in’) · also demonstrative gen. of comparison after a comparative: τοῦ γε κρεῖσσον ’better than this’ · also neut. gen. sg. in ἐκ τοῦ: ’from that time’ · also neut. gen. sg., partitive, ’of it’ (τοῦ μὲν ὅσον τ’ ὄργυιαν ’of it, about a fathom’) · also article-like with a noun: ’that, the’ (τοῦ παιδὸς ’that son’) · also article-like gen. sg. with a noun and a participle (gen. absolute), distributive: ’of the one … of the other’ (τοῦ μὲν φθίνοντος μηνός, τοῦ δ’ ἱσταμένοιο ’as one month wanes and the other begins’)
τοῦτον: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this; masc. acc. sg.
τρέφει: τρέφω — nourish, rear, foster; pres. 3 sg. (of Amphitrite fostering sea-creatures) · also of food, ’nourishes, makes thrive’ (τά θ’ ὕεσσι τρέφει τεθαλυῖαν ἀλοιφήν ’which nourishes thriving fat on pigs’)
τό: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun); neut. nom./acc. sg. ’it, that’; may anticipate a following clause: ’this (namely that…)’ · also relative, neut. acc. sg.: ’which’ (φάρμακον … τό σφιν πόρε ’the drug which she gave them’)
τὰ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’ · also in the adverbial idiom τὰ πρῶτα, ’at first, first’ (not ’these things’) · also with a noun, pointing to it: ’those, the’ (τὰ σὰ γούνατα ’those knees of yours’) · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: which; neut. nom. pl. (μῆλα, τὰ … κατάκειτ’ ’the flocks, which lie’) · also relative, neut. acc. pl.: ’which’, object of the verb in its clause (ῥωγαλέα, τὰ … ὅρηαι ’torn, which you see’)
τὴν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. acc. sg. ’her’ · also ’it’, of a thing (τὴν = the clothing): fem. acc. sg. · also with a noun, article-like: τὴν ὁδόν ’that journey’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whom; fem. acc. sg. (τὴν Ὠκεανὸς τέκε ’whom Oceanus begot’) · also ’the other’, contrasted with a preceding τὴν … μέν: fem. acc. sg. (τὴν δέ ’the other one’) · also article-like with a numeral: ’the one’ (τὴν μὲν ἴαν ’the one portion’)
τὸν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. acc. sg. ’him’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whom, which; masc. acc. sg. (τὸν Ἀλφειὸς τέκε ’whom Alpheus begot’) · also demonstrative adjective with a noun: ’that, the’ (τὸν μῦθον ’that story, message’) · also demonstrative, distributive: masc. acc. sg. ’the one … the other’ (τὸν μὲν … τὸν δ’) · also article-like with a participle: τὸν ἐόντα ’me, the one who am’ · also article-like with a superlative or ordinal: ’the best’ (τὸν ἄριστον), ’the fourth’ (τὸν τέταρτον) · also article-like with a substantivized adjective: ’the like (one)’ (τὸν ὁμοῖον)
τῇ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. dat. sg.: ’her, with her’ · also adverbial, ’there, in that place’, pointing back to a place just named (τῇ τόν γε μένον λοχόωντες ’there they lay in wait for him’) · also relative, fem. dat. sg., serving as an instrumental, ’with which’ (ῥάβδον, τῇ τ’ ἀνδρῶν ὄμματα θέλγει ’a wand, with which he charms men’s eyes’), not the personal pronoun · also relative adv., ’where, in the place where’ (τῇ δή μοι ἐείσατο χῶρος ἄριστος) · also adverbial, ’in that (event)’, pointing back to a contest just named: τῇ δ’ αὖτ’ Εὐρύαλος ἀπεκαίνυτο ’in that Euryalus in turn outdid all’ · also relative adv. of manner, with περ: ’in just the way that’ · also adv. of direction, ’thither, that way’ · also with a noun, article-like: fem. dat. sg. ’the’ (τῇ δεκάτῃ ’on the tenth’)
τῶν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); gen. pl. ’of these things, of them’ · also with a noun, article-like: τῶν ἄλλων ἀνέμων ’of the other winds’ · also distributive, ’of the one … of the other’ (τῶν μὲν … τῶν δ’ ’of the one band … of the other’) · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: gen. pl. ’of whom, whose’ (τῶν ὕβρις τε βίη τε … ἵκει ’whose insolence and violence reach’)
τῷ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc./neut. dat. sg.; also relative: ’in which’ · the relative dat. sg. also serves as an instrumental, ’with which’ (τῷ δάμνησι ’with which she overpowers’) · also adverbial ’therefore, and so’ (τῷ οὔ τινα οἶδα ’so I know no one’) · also article-like with a noun: ’that, the same’ (ἤματι τῷ αὐτῷ ’on that same day’) · also demonstrative instrumental, of a thing just named: ’with it’ (τῷ ἀπὸ πείσματ’ ἔκοψα ’with it I cut the cables off’) · also demonstrative of a thing just named, before a preposition: ’it’ (τῷ δ’ ἐν ’and on it’, τῷ δ’ ὑπό ’and beneath it’)
υἱέος: υἱός — son; masc. gen. sg. (υἱέος Ὀρτιλόχοιο ’son of Ortilochus’, in apposition to Diocles)
φάο: φημί — say, speak; pres. imper. mid. 2 sg., epic (= Attic φάθι): ’speak!’
φάτο: φημί — say, speak; impf. 3 sg. mid., unaugmented (= ἔφατο)
φίλην: φίλος — dear, one’s own; fem. acc. sg.
φίλοιο: φίλος — dear; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
φίλον: φίλος — dear, one’s own (with kin/body parts serves as a possessive); neut. nom./acc. sg. · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with a masculine noun: φίλον υἱόν ’dear son’ · also masc. acc. sg. predicative, agreeing with a pronoun: ’as a friend, welcome’ (φίλον ἐλθεῖν)
φίλων: φίλος — dear, one’s own; masc. gen. pl. (φίλοι ’kin, dear ones’) · also attributive with ἑταίρων: ’dear (companions)’ (φίλων … ἑταίρων)
φαμένη: φημί — say, speak; pres. part. mid. fem. nom. sg.: ’so saying’
φανῆναι: φαίνω — show; pass. appear; aor. pass. inf.: ’to appear’
φημὶ: φημί — say, assert, declare; pres. 1 sg.
φρεσὶ: φρήν — mind, heart, wits; fem. dat. pl.
φύγε: φεύγω — flee, escape; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔφυγε); + acc.: ’fled from’
φώνησέν: φωνέω — utter, speak aloud, call out; aor. 3 sg., accented φώνησέν before the enclitic τε
χαρίτων: Χάρις — Grace, one of the goddesses of charm; fem. gen. pl.
χαῖρε: χαίρω — rejoice; pres. imper. 2 sg., the ordinary greeting: ’welcome, hail’ · also impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔχαιρε): ’he rejoiced’ (χαῖρε φήμῃ ’rejoiced at the omen-word’) · also the imperative at parting: ’farewell’ · also with a dative of cause, ’be glad’ (χαῖρε … φιλότητι ’be glad in love’)
χερσὶ: χείρ — hand; fem. dat. pl., epic -σί (= Attic χερσίν)
χορὸν: χορός — dance; dancing-place; masc. acc. sg.
χρυσέῳ: χρύσεος — golden; neut. dat. sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic χρυσῷ)
ἀείρας: ἀείρω — lift, raise (Attic αἴρω); aor. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’having lifted’
ἀεικέα: ἀεικής — unseemly, shameful, unfitting; masc. acc. sg. · also neut. acc. pl., used substantivally: ’unseemly things’ (ἀεικέα μερμηρίζων ’pondering unseemly things’) · also fem. acc. sg., agreeing with πήρην: ’unseemly, shabby (wallet)’ · also neut. acc. pl., attributive: ’shameful (deeds)’ (ἀεικέα ἔργ’) · also fem. acc. sg. (one form for masc. and fem.), agreeing with πήρην: ’unseemly’ (ἀεικέα πήρην ’an unseemly wallet’)
ἀθάνατοι: ἀθάνατος — immortal, deathless; masc. nom. pl.: ’the immortals’
ἀθήνη: Ἀθήνη — Athena, goddess of wisdom and war; nom. sg.
ἀθανάτοισι: ἀθάνατος — immortal, deathless; masc. dat. pl., epic (= Attic -οις)
ἀμφ: ἀμφί (elided ἀμφ’) — around, about, concerning; + dat. · also + acc., ’around, with, accompanying’ (ἀμφ’ Ὀδυσῆα ’with, around Odysseus’) · also + gen., ’about, concerning’ (ἀμφ’ Ἄρεος φιλότητος ’about the love of Ares’) · also with ὀστεόφιν, ’around’ (ἀμφ’ ὀστεόφιν θὶς ’a heap around the bones’)
ἀμφίνομος: Ἀμφίνομος — Amphinomus, one of the suitors; masc. nom. sg.
ἀμφίπολοι: ἀμφίπολος — handmaid, attendant; fem. nom. pl. · also fem. voc. pl., address: ’handmaids!’
ἀμφίπολος: ἀμφίπολος — handmaid, woman in attendance; nom. sg.
ἀμφὶ: ἀμφί — on both sides, around, about; prep./adv. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἀμφὶ ... βάλλομεν = ἀμφιβάλλομεν ’we threw around, embraced’)
ἀνέρας: ἀνήρ — man; masc. acc. pl., epic ἀνέρας (= Attic ἄνδρας)
ἀνέστη: ἀνίστημι — stand up, rise; aor. 3 sg. intrans.: ’stood up’
ἀνακλινθεῖσα: ἀνακλίνω — lean back, cause to recline; aor. pass. part. fem. nom. sg.
ἀνθρώπων: ἄνθρωπος — human being, man; gen. pl.
ἀντίνοος: Ἀντίνοος — Antinous, son of Eupeithes, a leading suitor; masc. nom. sg.
ἀνῆκε: ἀνίημι — send up, rouse, stir (to something); aor. 3 sg., the gnomic aorist of a general truth
ἀορτήρ: ἀορτήρ — strap, sling (by which a bag hangs); masc. nom. sg.
ἀπαμειβόμενος: ἀπαμείβομαι — answer, reply; pres. part. nom. sg. masc.
ἀπομόρξατο: ἀπομόργνυμι — wipe off; mid. wipe from oneself; aor. 3 sg. mid.: ’wiped away’
ἀρετὴν: ἀρετή — excellence, worth; fem. acc. sg.
ἀτάσθαλα: ἀτάσθαλος — wanton, reckless; neut. acc. pl., substantive: ’wanton, reckless deeds’, the adjective behind the fixed noun ἀτασθαλίαι ’wanton-follies’
ἀτὰρ: ἀτάρ — but, and; epic conj. (by-form of αὐτάρ)
ἀφίκετο: ἀφικνέομαι — arrive at, reach; aor. 3 sg.
ἀχαιοί: Ἀχαιοί — the Achaeans, the Greeks; masc. nom. pl.
ἀχαιῶν: Ἀχαιοί — the Achaeans, the Greeks; gen. pl.
ἁγνὴ: ἁγνός — pure, holy, chaste; fem. nom. sg.
ἂν: ἄν — modal particle marking contingency (with subj. = future contingency, with opt. = potential) · also with a secondary indicative (impf./aor.) marking an unreal, contrary-to-fact conclusion: ’would’ (οὐκ ἂν ... ἀγόρευες ’you would not be speaking’) · also = ἀνά (preposition/preverb ’up’) in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἂν … βαῖνε = ἀνέβαινε, ἂν … βάντες = ἀναβάντες) · also = ἀνά as a preposition + acc.: ’up through, up among’ (ἂν δόνακας ’up through the reeds’) · also in ὡς ἄν + opt., a purpose clause: ’so that … might’ (ὡς ἂν … ἑλοίμεθα ’so that we might seize’)
ἄκουον: ἀκούω — hear; impf. 3 pl., unaugmented (= ἤκουον) · also impf. 1 sg., unaugmented (= ἤκουον): ’I used to hear’
ἄκουσον: ἀκούω — hear, listen; aor. imper. 2 sg., + gen.: ’hear (me)’
ἄλλ: ἄλλος — other, another; neut. acc. sg., elided (ἄλλ’ = ἄλλο): ’another thing’ · also neut. nom./acc. pl. ἄλλα, elided, genuinely ambiguous with the sg. reading: ἄλλ’ ἐνόησεν ’devised other things’ or ’another thing’ · also the conjunction ἀλλά ’but’, elided, as printed before ἄγε: ἄλλ’ ἄγε δή ’but come now’
ἄλλοι: ἄλλος — other, another; masc. nom. pl.
ἄμβροτα: ἄμβροτος — immortal, divine, undying; adj., neut. acc. pl., epic (= ἀθάνατος)
ἄνωχθι: ἄνωγα — bid, command; perf. imper. 2 sg.: ’bid! order!’
ἄρ: ἄρα — then, so, as it seems; inferential particle, elided form ἄρ’ before a vowel · also the shortened form ἄρ used, without true elision, before τε in the fixed collocation ἄρ τε: τὰ μὲν ἄρ τε διεσκέδασ’
ἄρα: ἄρα — so, as it turned out, then; inferential particle
ἄρτεμις: Ἄρτεμις — Artemis, goddess of the hunt and of sudden painless death (esp. of women); fem. nom. sg.
ἅμα: ἅμα — together with, at the same time as; adv./prep. + dat.
ἅψεα: ἅψεα — limbs, joints (Attic ἄρθρα/μέλη), often paired with λύω of sleep or death; neut. nom./acc. pl.
ἐέλδεται: ἐέλδομαι — long for, wish; pres. 3 sg. mid., epic with prothetic ἐ- (= Attic ἐπιθυμεῖ), + inf.
ἐγώ: ἐγώ — I; nom. sg. (accented ἐγώ before the enclitic τοι that follows) · also accented ἐγώ before the enclitic μιν that follows · also accented before the enclitic τε: σύ τ’ ἐγώ τε ’you and I’
ἐθέλεις: ἐθέλω — wish, be willing, intend; pres. 2 sg.
ἐκ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as adverb or preverb in tmesis, no case expressed: ’out’ (ἐκ δ’ ἔβαν ’and out they stepped’)
ἐκείνῳ: κεῖνος (Attic ἐκεῖνος) — that, that one; demonstrative pron., masc. dat. sg.
ἐλθέμεν: ἔρχομαι — go, come; aor. inf., epic ἐλθέμεν (= Attic ἐλθεῖν): ’to come’
ἐμοί: ἐγώ — I; dat. sg., accented (non-enclitic emphatic): ’to me’
ἐμοῖσι: ἐμός — my, mine; masc./neut. dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic ἐμοῖς)
ἐμῷ: ἐμός — my, mine; masc. dat. sg.
ἐν: ἐν — in, on, among; + dat.; also used as an adverb, ’in it, there’ · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐν … βάλῃ = ἐμβάλῃ ’cast in’; ἐν … χεῦον = ἔγχεον ’pour in’)
ἐνόησε: νοέω — perceive, think, devise; aor. 3 sg.
ἐνὶ: ἐν (epic ἐνί) — in, on, among; + dat. · also adverb or preverb, no case: ’therein’ (ἔνθ’ ἐνὶ πέπλοι ... βεβλήατο ’therein coverlets were laid’) · also + gen., of a person’s house: ’in the house of’ (ἐνὶ Κίρκης ’in Circe’s house’)
ἐξ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐξ … ἕντο = ἐξέντο, from ἐξίημι ’send out, put away (desire)’)
ἐπ: ἐπί (elided ἐπ’) — on, upon, over, towards, against; + dat./acc./gen. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐπ’ … χεῦε = ἐπέχευε ‘poured upon’) · also + dat., of time: ’in, within’ (ἐπ’ ἤματι ’in a day’) · also + acc., ’in pursuit of, after’ (ἐπ’ ἀγροτέρας ’after wild (goats)’) · also + dat., ’in favour of, on behalf of’ (ἐπ’ Ἴρῳ ἦρα φέρων ’showing favour to Irus’)
ἐπέεσσι: ἔπος — word, speech; neut. dat. pl., epic -εσσι (= Attic ἔπεσι)
ἐπίκευθε: ἐπικεύθω — hide, conceal; pres. imper. act. 2 sg., in a prohibition with μηδέ: ’do not hide (it)’
ἐπιχθονίων: ἐπιχθόνιος — upon the earth (epithet of mortals, as against the gods); masc./fem. gen. pl.
ἐπὶ: ἐπί — on, upon, over, towards, against; + dat./acc./gen. · also as adverb, no case expressed: ’to it, over it; besides’ (θεοὶ δ’ ἐπὶ μάρτυροι ’witnesses to it’; ἐπὶ κτέρεα κτερεΐξαι ’besides’) · also + dat., ’beyond, over and above, more than’ (ἐπὶ γαστέρι κύντερον ’more shameless than the belly’) · also adverb of sequence, ’next, thereupon’ (ἦλθε δ’ ἐπὶ ψυχή ’and next came the soul’) · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb: ἐπὶ … τέταλτο = ἐπιτέταλτο ’was laid upon, entrusted’ · also + acc. of time: ’for, over’ (ἐπὶ χρόνον ’for a time’) · also + dat., ’in charge of, over’ (ἐπὶ κτεάτεσσιν ’over my possessions’) · also + dat., of purpose: ’for’ (ἐπὶ δόρπῳ ’for supper’)
ἐρέω: ἐρέω — say, tell, declare; fut. 1 sg. (epic fut. of εἶπον, = Attic ἐρῶ); in tmesis with ἐκ, ἐξερέω ’speak out plainly’
ἐς: εἰς (epic ἐς) — into, to; + acc. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb with no case expressed (ἐς … ἦλθον = εἰσῆλθον ’came in’)
ἐσθλὸν: ἐσθλός — good, noble, brave; neut./masc. acc. sg.
ἔβη: βαίνω — go, walk, step; aor. 3 sg., root aorist, unaugmented (= ἔβη)
ἔειπεν: εἶπον — say, speak; aor. 3 sg., epic augmented (ἔ-ειπεν, = Attic εἶπεν)
ἔειπες: εἶπον — say, speak; aor. 2 sg., epic uncontracted, augment ἐ- kept (ἔειπες = εἶπες)
ἔθηκε: τίθημι — put, place, cause, bring about; aor. 3 sg., augmented (root θη-/θε-, consonant-initial; unaugmented θῆκε): ’set, caused’ (ἔριν ἔθηκε ’set strife’)
ἔκ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; prep. + gen., placed after its pronoun with anastrophe: τοῦ ... ἔκ = ἐκ τοῦ ’from him’ · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἔκ … ὀνόμαζε = ἐξωνόμαζε ’called by name’) · also prep. + gen. with a particle between it and its noun: ἔκ γε γυναικός ’at the hands of a woman’
ἔμελλον: μέλλω — be about to, be destined to; impf. 3 pl. · also impf. 1 sg. (same form): ’I was destined, was about to’ + fut. inf.
ἔμεν: εἰμί — be; pres. inf., epic, shortened (= Attic εἶναι; cf. ἔμμεναι) · also μένω — stay, wait; impf. 3 sg., elided, augmented (ἔμεν’ = ἔμενε): ’he waited’
ἔμπης: ἔμπης — nevertheless, in any case, for all that; adv.
ἔνθ: ἔνθα (elided ἔνθ’) — there, then; adverb of place or time
ἔνθεν: ἔνθεν — from there, thence; adv. of place, with suffix -θεν · also ’on the one side’ (ἔνθεν μὲν γὰρ πέτραι ’on one side are rocks’)
ἔοικας: ἔοικα — be like, resemble (+ dat.); perf. 2 sg. with pres. sense: ’you are like’
ἔπι: ἐπί — on, upon, over; prep. + dat., placed after its noun with anastrophe: ἑοῖς ἔπι ’upon his own (possessions)’ · also + gen., postpositive with anastrophe, of direction: ’toward’ (νήσου ἔπι Ψυρίης ’toward the island of Psyria’) · also as adverb with no case expressed, intensifying repetition: ’besides, again’ (ἔπι δεύτερον αὖτις ’a second time, once more’) · also = ἔπεστι, accented on the first syllable when it stands for the verb: ’there is (upon)’ · also as preverb in tmesis, placed after its object: ἔπι … ὦρσεν = ἐπῶρσεν ’stirred up (against)’ · also + gen., postpositive with anastrophe, of place: ’on, upon’ (οὐδοῦ ἔπι ξεστοῦ ’on the polished threshold’)
ἔπλετο: πέλομαι — be, become, happen; aor. 3 sg. used with pres. force: ’is’ · also with ordinary past/aorist force: ’came to be, arose’ (τοῦτο νόημα ἔπλετο ’this thought has arisen’)
ἔπος: ἔπος — word, speech, thing said; neut. nom./acc. sg.
ἔρεξα: ῥέζω — do, perform; esp. offer sacrifice; aor. 1 sg.
ἔρχευ: ἔρχομαι — go, come; imper. 2 sg., epic ἔρχευ (= Attic ἔρχου)
ἔς: εἰς (epic ἐς) — into, to; prep. + acc.
ἔφαν: φημί — say; impf./aor. 3 pl., epic (= Attic ἔφασαν): ’they said’
ἔφατ: φημί — say, speak; impf. 3 sg. mid., augmented, elided (ἔφατ’ = ἔφατο)
ἔχετον: Ἔχετος — Echetus, a cruel king of the mainland; masc. acc. sg.
ἔχευεν: χέω — pour; aor. 3 sg., in tmesis with ἐν (ἐν … ἔχευεν = ἐνέχευεν): ’poured in’ · also in tmesis with κατά (κατὰ … ἔχευεν = κατέχευεν): ’poured down, shed’
ἔχοι: ἔχω — have, hold; pres. opt. 3 sg.
ἕζετ: ἕζομαι — sit down; impf. 3 sg., elided (ἕζετ’ = ἕζετο), in tmesis with κατά: ’sat down’ · also plain, no tmesis: ’sat’ (ἕζετ’ ἔπειτ’ ἐπὶ θῖνα ’then sat down on the shore’)
ἠρήσαντο: ἀράομαι — pray, wish; aor. mid. 3 pl.
ἡ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. nom. sg.: ’she’ · also fem. nom. sg. ’it’, of a pool of water (ἡ δὲ προσέπλαζε ’and it lapped up’) · also fem. nom. sg. ’it’, of a ship (ἡ δ’ ἔθει ’and it ran’) · also fem. nom. sg. with a noun/adj., article-like: ’the other’ (ἡ δ’ ἄλλη ’and the other woman’) · also fem. nom. sg. article-like with a noun: ’the’ (ἡ γὰρ δμώων δίκη ’for the way of servants’)
ἡδὺ: ἡδύς — sweet, pleasant; adj., neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’sweetly’ · also attributive, agreeing with a neut. noun: ’sweet’ (ἡδὺ ποτόν ’sweet drink’)
ἢ: ἤ — or; disjunctive conj. (epic ἠέ/ἤ) · also ’than’ after a comparative: κρεῖσσον … ἢ ὅτε ’better than when’ · also ’before’ after a verb of anticipating (ἔφθης … ἢ ἐγώ ’you got here before I did’) · also introducing the first alternative of an indirect question: ’whether’ (ἢ ἔτι … ἦέ τις ’whether still … or someone’) · also ’than’ after a verb of preferring: βουλοίμην … ἢ … ἀνάσσειν ’I would rather … than rule’ · also introducing the first alternative of a deliberation: ’whether … or’ (ἢ ἐλάσει’ … ἦέ μιν ἦκ’ ἐλάσειε)
ἤδη: ἤδη — now, already, at once; adv.
ἤπειρόνδε: ἤπειρος — mainland; fem. acc. sg. + directional suffix -δε: ’to the mainland’
ἦ: ἦ — truly, verily; affirming particle · also interrogative particle introducing an earnest question · also = ἤ ’or’, in the correlative ἠέ … ἦ ’whether … or’ · also ἠμί — say, speak; unaugmented aor./impf. 3 sg. (= ἔφη), closing or introducing direct speech: ’he/she said’ (ἦ ῥα ’so he said’) · also ’or’, the second alternative of a pair of questions with no preceding ἠέ: ζώει … ἦ τέθνηκε ’alive or dead’; ἢ ἔτ’ ἔχει … ἦ μιν ἀτιμάζουσιν ’whether … or’
ἦεν: εἰμί — be; impf. 3 sg., epic (= Attic ἦν)
ἦλθον: ἔρχομαι — go, come; aor. 3 pl.: ’they came’ · also aor. 1 sg. (the same ending serves both persons): ’I have come’
ἦμαρ: ἦμαρ — day (epic for ἡμέρα); neut. nom./acc. sg.
ἰδέσθαι: ὁράω — see; aor. mid. inf.: ‘to see’
ἰδὲ: ἰδέ — and; epic conj. (= Attic καί)
ἰκαρίοιο: Ἰκάριος — Icarius, father of Penelope; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
ἰὼν: εἶμι — go; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’going’
ἱμερόεντα: ἱμερόεις — lovely, charming, arousing longing (ἵμερος ’longing’); neut. acc. pl. (with ἔπεα)
ἴσαν: εἶμι — go, come; impf. 3 pl., epic: ’used to go, come’ · also as a simple narrative past, ’went’ (μνηστῆρες … ἴσαν ’the suitors went’), not necessarily iterative · also οἶδα — know; unaugmented plup. 3 pl. with impf. sense, epic (= Attic ᾔδεσαν): ’they knew’ (τὰ δ’ οὐκ ἴσαν ’they did not know’)
ἴῃ: εἶμι — go; pres. subj. 3 sg., after ὄφρα: ’may go’
ἵνα: ἵνα — so that, in order that; + subj. · also + opt. after a past tense · also relative ’where’ + indic.: ἵνα … καθεύδετον ’where the two are sleeping’ · also + opt. after a future main verb: ’so that … may’ (ἄξω … ἵνα … ἄλφοι ’I will take … so that he may bring in’)
ἶφι: ἶφι — mightily, by force; adv. (instrumental -φι of ἴς)
ὀΐω: ὀΐομαι — think, suppose; pres. 1 sg. (act. form ὀΐω, epic; = Attic οἴομαι): ’I think’
ὀδυρομένη: ὀδύρομαι — lament, mourn for; pres. part. fem. nom. sg.
ὀδυσσεύς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus, the poem’s hero; nom. sg.
ὀνόμαζεν: ὀνομάζω — call by name, name; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= Attic ὠνόμαζε); with ἐκ in tmesis (ἔκ … ὀνόμαζεν) ’called by name’
ὀπίσσω: ὀπίσσω — behind; in Homer also ’hereafter, in time to come’; adv. · also ’back, home again’, of return (οἴκαδ’ ὀπίσσω ’back home’)
ὀτρυνέουσα: ὀτρύνω — urge on, rouse; fut. part. act., fem. nom. sg., epic uncontracted -έουσα (= Attic ὀτρυνοῦσα), of purpose: ’to urge on’
ὁ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. nom. sg. · also article-like with an adjective and a name: ’the’ (ὁ θρασὺς Ὀδυσσεύς ’bold Odysseus’) · also article-like with a noun: ’the’ (ὁ γέρων ’the old man’) · also distributive, masc. nom. sg.: ’the one’ (ὁ μὲν οὐρανὸν εὐρὺν ἱκάνει ’the one reaches the broad heaven’) · also article-like with a superlative: ’the worst’ (ὁ κάκιστος Ἀχαιῶν ’the worst of the Achaeans’)
ὁππότε: ὁππότε (Attic ὁπότε) — whenever, when; conj., + subj. and κε in a general temporal clause · also introducing an indirect question, + pres. indic.: ’when’ (ὁππότε Τηλέμαχος νεῖτ(αι) ’when Telemachus is to return’) · also + subj. without κε, in a general clause: ’whenever’ (ὁππότε τις μνήσῃ ’whenever anyone mentions’)
ὁρόω: ὁράω — see; pres. 1 sg., epic stretched form (= Attic ὁρῶ)
ὃν: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; masc./neut. acc. sg. · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: whom, which (masc. acc. sg.)
ὃς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (relative) — who, which; masc. nom. sg. · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own (masc. nom. sg.) · also plain demonstrative, ’he’ (ὃς γὰρ δεύτατος ἦλθεν), not a relative
ὄλβιος: ὄλβιος — blessed, fortunate, prosperous; masc. nom. sg.
ὄλυμπον: Ὄλυμπος — Olympus, home of the gods; masc. acc. sg.
ὄπιθεν: ὄπιθεν — from behind, hereafter, in time to come; adv., with the directional suffix -θεν · also ’behind’, of those left at home, no motion from (τῶν ὄπιθεν ’those behind’) · also with a verb of going, ’off behind’ (ἰὼν ὄπιθεν ’going off behind’)
ὄσσετο: ὄσσομαι — forebode, see in the mind; impf. 3 sg. mid., a Homeric word with no Attic equivalent: ’boded, foreboded’
ὄφρ: ὄφρα (elided ὄφρ’) — so that, in order that; epic (= Attic ἵνα); + subj. · also temporal, ’as long as, while’ + indicative (ὄφρ’ ἔτι κεῖνος ἀνὴρ ἐπιδήμιος ἦεν ’as long as that man was still at home’) · also ’while’ + ἄν and subj. · also temporal ’until’ + indicative (ὄφρ’ ἵκετ’ Ἀρήτην ’until he came to Arete’) · also ’until’ + ἄν and subj. (ὄφρ’ ἂν ἵκηαι ’until you reach’) · also + opt. in a purpose clause after a secondary verb: ’so that … might’ (ὄφρ’ … μένοιεν) · also temporal ’until’ + opt., of a hoped-for event (ὄφρ’ ἐξεμέσειεν ’until she should vomit out’) · also ὄφρ’ ἂν + opt., ’until … should’ (ὄφρ’ ἂν ἄγοιεν ’until they should carry’)
ὄφρα: ὄφρα — so that, in order that; epic (= Attic ἵνα); + subj. · also temporal, ’until’, + indic. (ὄφρα ... βάλε): marking the point an action ceases · also temporal + subj. with κε, correlative with τόφρα: ’as long as, until’ (ὄφρα κε κείνη τοῦτον ἔχῃ νόον ’for as long as she holds this purpose’) · also + opt. in a purpose clause after a secondary-sequence verb: ὄφρα ... ἕλοις/ἵκοιο ’so that you might take/arrive’ · also temporal + indic., ’as long as’ (ὄφρα μὲν … ἦν ’so long as it was’)
ὅ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. sg.; with γε: ’he’ · also relative, masc. nom. sg., accented before an enclitic: ’who’ (ὅ κε ... ἐφείη) · also = ὅτι ’that’; εἰς ὅ ’until’ · also relative, neut. nom./acc. sg.: ’which’ (ὅ οἱ πέρι δῶκεν Ἀθήνη ’which Athena gave her beyond others’) · also masc. nom. sg. pronoun ’he’ without γε, accented before an enclitic (ὅ σφιν ’he … to them’)
ὅπως: ὅπως — so that, in order that, how; + subj. or fut. indic. · also + opt., in secondary sequence after a past-tense verb, indirect deliberative: ’how it might’ (ὅπως ἄριστα γένοιτο ’how it might turn out best’) · also ’when’ = ὅτε · also ’as, however’ + subj. in a general clause: ὅπως ἐθέλῃσιν ’however he wishes’ · also + opt. in a purpose clause after a past tense: ’so that … might follow’ (ὅπως … ἑποίατο) · also + pres. indic., ’as, in whatever way’ (ὅπως ἐθέλεις ’as you wish’) · also ’how’ + aor. indic., indirect question after a verb of telling (κατάλεξον ὅπως ἤντησας ’tell how you came upon’)
ὅσσα: ὅσος — as much/many as; epic ὅσσος (double σ), neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’as many as’
ὅτε: ὅτε — when; temporal conjunction · also ’since, now that’ (ὅτε πρότερός γε πύθοιτο ’since he learned of it first’) · also with the optative, hypothetical/conditional: ’if ever, whenever’ (ὅτε ... ἵκοι ’if ever such need should come upon me’) · also with the subjunctive, general: ’whenever’ (ὅτε στείχῃσ’ ἀνὰ ἄστυ ’whenever she goes through the town’) · also with the optative, iterative in past time: ’whenever’ (ὅτε μέλλοι ’whenever he was about to’) · also with the pres. indic., ’whereas, when’ (ὅτε τ’ ἄλλοι ἅπαξ θνῄσκουσ’ ἄνθρωποι ’whereas other men die only once’) · also in ὅτε μή, ’unless, except when’ (ὅτε μὴ θεὸς … θείη ’unless a god should make’)
ὅττι: ὅστις — whoever, whatever; epic neut. nom./acc. sg. ὅττι (= Attic ὅ τι) · also with a superlative, ’as … as possible’ (ὅττι τάχιστα ’as quickly as possible’) · also in an indirect question, ’what’ (ὅττι ἑ κήδοι ’what was troubling him’) · also conj. ’that, because’, introducing a clause (ὅττι μιν ὣς ὑπέδεκτο ’that he had received him so’)
ὑπερφιάλοισιν: ὑπερφίαλος — overweening, arrogant; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οις)
ὑπερώϊα: ὑπερῷον — upper room, upper storey; neut. pl., epic ὑπερώϊα (= Attic ὑπερῷα), acc. of goal
ὑπὸ: ὑπό — under, beneath; prep. + dat./acc.; also used as an adverb, ’beneath’ · also as preverb in tmesis (ὑπὸ … ἐδήσατο = ὑπεδήσατο ’bound beneath’) · also adverbial, of breeding: ’begotten under, born of’ (ὑπὸ δ’ ἡμίονοι ’and under them [the mares], mules’) · also + dat., marking the agent with a passive verb: ’by’ (ὑπὸ μνηστῆρσιν δαμείη ’be overcome by the suitors’) · also + gen., ’from under, beneath’ (ὑπὸ στέρνοιο) · also + gen., marking agent with a passive verb/participle beyond dying, ’by’: μεγάλου ὑπὸ κύματος ἀρθείς ’lifted up by a great wave’ · also + gen., of cause: ὑπὸ ῥιπῆς ’at the rush (of the throw)’
ὣς: ὥς — thus, so; adverb (accented, distinct from unaccented ὡς ’as’; = Attic οὕτως) · also postpositive after its noun (anastrophe), = comparative ὡς ’as, like’: ὄρνις δ’ ὥς ’like a bird’
ὤμοισιν: ὦμος — shoulder; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οις)
ῥ: ἄρα (weakened ῥα, elided ῥ’) — then, indeed, so; inferential particle
ῥα: ἄρα — then, so; weak enclitic form ῥα (used after a vowel)
ῥωγαλέην: ῥωγαλέος — ragged, torn; fem. acc. sg.
